sources.quote:
How much AI is used? I'm just curious
is02ac View Profile View Posts [developer] Oct 18 @ 12:49am Report this post Hi, I used it for programming and translating from French (sometimes I write directly in English, but not every time) #1
Žaidikas View Profile View Posts Oct 18 @ 1:05am Report this post Originally posted by is02ac : Hi, I used it for programming and translating from French (sometimes I write directly in English, but not every time) Thanks for response. I can tolerate for programming. #2
spitfire_ch View Profile View Posts 1 Oct 26 @ 8:33am Report this post I'm also just curious: why is it OK for programming but not for art? I'm actually a SQL developer (Data Analyst/Engineer), and my job is as much at stake as an artist's — probably even more so. I try to embrace AI as much as possible to avoid being left behind. In my opinion, it's OK to use AI for programming and everything else. Unless you use the environment argument, in which case it's not OK for anything, and I am very much guilty myself. But I don't get why artists always are the big victims in the AI world. #3
is02ac View Profile View Posts [developer] Oct 26 @ 9:14am Report this post Originally posted by spitfire_ch : I'm also just curious: why is it OK for programming but not for art? I'm actually a SQL developer (Data Analyst/Engineer), and my job is as much at stake as an artist's — probably even more so. I try to embrace AI as much as possible to avoid being left behind. In my opinion, it's OK to use AI for programming and everything else. Unless you use the environment argument, in which case it's not OK for anything, and I am very much guilty myself. But I don't get why artists always are the big victims in the AI world. I'm a video game student in a game design school at Isart digital Paris. In this school we also have game artists and sound designers that have huge difficulties to find jobs, because of the current situation of the video game industry. Generated art from AI is mainly art stole from artists that never wanted this tool. So for that main reason I prefere pay commercial license of real artist (like I did for the artwork of the inspector Reye, for the sound, it's a free licence). But for the programmation, AI created more jobs than it deleted them (In France at least). Secondly, depending on how you use it, programming don't remove the creative part of making a game. For the translation, i'm a bit frustated to use AI, but I prefere that than don't translate anything. For now i didn't received any money so I can't afford for translation compagny, but maybe after the release I will contact it to arrange that part of the game. #4
Žaidikas View Profile View Posts Oct 26 @ 9:37am Report this post Originally posted by spitfire_ch : I'm also just curious: why is it OK for programming but not for art? In my opinion, it's OK to use AI for programming and everything else. Unless you use the environment argument, in which case it's not OK for anything, and I am very much guilty myself. But I don't get why artists always are the big victims in the AI world. First of all just look how easy and effortless is to make something with AI. Anyone who never touch the pencil in his life can create digital art now wihtout talent, work or effort. Why to pay for it? What value it has. Secondly art is the thing we see in game and interact with, code is like backend. Of course i'm against AI in all aspects of game creation. Last edited by Žaidikas ; Oct 26 @ 12:10pm #5
nomadredd View Profile View Posts Oct 27 @ 3:35am Report this post Are gamers/people dont like AI? I do professional SQL development and we use AI for queries now too. AI is just the way to go these days, more productive. Though the modelling and business analyst part of the work still requires real humans to think and validate. I have used AI much in the development and it's just a tool like a calculator. At the end of the day, one's work speaks for itself if it is good or slop, regardless if it was doing 100% by people or not. #6
Cilvaa View Profile View Posts 1 Oct 29 @ 1:33am Report this post Originally posted by spitfire_ch : I'm also just curious: why is it OK for programming but not for art? Art is by nature creative. Coding, like any language, has rules. While yes you could write several versions of code in the same language, and achieve the same result; ultimately it all falls back on structured rules. If I ask 100 coders to build a basic web UI based on a layout sketch and a list of requirements, they might lay things out very differently, use different CSS properties for styling, use different colours and fonts, different CSS templates; but core components will be coded nearly identically. Certain systems need to be written a specific way just to function. If I ask an AI to create an API that can read data from a SharePoint list, it doesn't need to "create" it, there is documentation on the Microsoft website it can follow to write it. If you asked a human to do it, and they didn't already know how, they'll read the same documentation and arrive at a near-identical result. That's not very creative of the AI, that's just following the instructions. And it doesn't need to steal ideas from programmers, documentation for languages and things like APIs are very accessible. If an AI doesn't know how to do something, it can literally just read the manual. If I ask 100 artists to "draw a cat sitting at a window", I will get 100 quite different drawings. That is truely creative because that is a vague set of parameters and they can use any mediums they want, paper or digital, pencil or pen, black and white or colour, realistic or cartoony, viewing the cat from inside the window or outside, with perspective or orthographic, etc. Last edited by Cilvaa ; Oct 29 @ 1:35am #7

Please hire a translation company if this game does well enough! I love the story bits! #8

That is truely creative because that is a vague set of parameters and they can use any mediums they want, paper or digital, pencil or pen, black and white or colour, realistic or cartoony, viewing the cat from inside the window or outside, with perspective or orthographic, etc. I think several coders would not create totally different code many many times. If you ask them to write a function, yes, they will be similar, but if you ask them to code the same application they will think different architectures with different components, so they will need different code in them. There are a ton of ways to solve the same problem. The main difference between art and coding in the AI subject is that nobody can do all the code of a program without the design of what they want and some insight about how to create a program. They still hire coders to code with AI. But with art and translations they don't hire artists, I think. Also images are created by copying images while language is different, AI can create text of its own, the original texts or programs used in training are much more diluted and it can create texts that never existed before. #9
spitfire_ch View Profile View Posts Oct 30 @ 3:42am Report this post AI creates images from scratch by learning mathematical patterns and concepts, exactly the same way it generates code or text. It doesn't copy or store source images—it uses them as learning material, much like a human artist studies the work of others to build their own style. #10
